investigation_notes.Hash Reputation Summary: No detections across available engines and community score is 0, indicating no known public detections for this binary.
investigation_notes.Decoded Script Summary: The PowerShell command creates a System.Net.Sockets.TCPClient to 45.33.19.121:443 and implements a reverse shell that reads commands from the socket and invokes them via iex, indicating interactive remote command execution.
investigation_notes.Description: A PowerShell-based reverse TCP shell was executed from winword.exe on the workstation, with the parent process being outlook.exe, which strongly suggests a malicious Office macro or weaponized document delivered via email. External indicators (45.33.19.121 on port 443) point to a public Linode-hosted endpoint and the initiating binary has no public detections, but the behavior of spawning an interactive remote shell from Word is highly anomalous and indicative of compromise. Given the direct remote command execution capability, lack of benign contextual justification, and the execution chain through Outlook/Word, this activity is classified as High Priority for immediate escalation.
